name: container-image-smoke
description: Drives the external binaries the container image ships (rsvg-convert, ffmpeg) from a real recipe on a real pseudo-terminal, and asserts on what they produced.
intent: Prove the published image can run a recipe end to end, not just answer --help.

argv: set -eu; rsvg-convert --output panel.png panel.svg; printf 'rasterised %s bytes\n' "$(wc -c < panel.png | tr -d ' ')"; ffmpeg -nostdin -loglevel error -y -loop 1 -i panel.png -t 1 -r 8 -c:v mpeg4 -pix_fmt yuv420p clip.mp4; printf 'encoded %s bytes\n' "$(wc -c < clip.mp4 | tr -d ' ')"; echo SMOKE-OK

steps.name: reach the end of the script

assertions.name: the script ran to completion on the terminal
no tool wrote a zero-byte artifact

checks: rsvg-convert is installed and rasterises an SVG the renderer could have emitted
ffmpeg is installed and encodes a video stream
a pseudo-terminal can be allocated inside the container
